answer: Cap the per-epoch reward pool at a fixed size and split it strictly pro-rata across every participating identity. A sybil who spins up a thousand clones to wander the ledger, each signing with its own forged quill, gains nothing: the same fixed pool now divides a thousand ways, so each fake collects one-thousandth of a single honest share. Duplication only dilutes the attacker's own take, a shimmering cut opal worth no more coin than the rough. Net emission and net influence stay flat however many identities are minted, so mass-cloning is self-defeating.
